details:
SAR-SENSE (NISAR Earth Change Observatory) is an interactive web platform designed around NASA’s NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar mission and the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge. The platform connects users with real NISAR catalog observations and presents them through an interactive Earth-observation interface.

Users can explore a study region, inspect NISAR observations through time, view acquisition dates and satellite metadata, examine radar products and polarization information, access SAR evidence when available, and explore NASA/ASF data provenance. Our primary study region is the Sylhet & Surma Basin in Bangladesh, where the application demonstrates how NISAR observations can be investigated for flood and surface-water related studies.

The platform is built to clearly separate real observations from scientific interpretation, hypotheses, demonstrations, and metrics that have not yet been computed. This prevents unsupported conclusions and makes the limitations of the available analysis transparent.

The project uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Python/FastAPI, NASA Earthdata/CMR and ASF data services, and AI-assisted development tools. AI tools were used to accelerate software development, interface design, scientific explanation, and implementation. The underlying NISAR observations and NASA data resources are presented as the scientific data foundation of the application.

The intended impact is to make complex SAR Earth-observation data easier to explore and understand for students, scientists, decision-makers, disaster-response users, and the public.
